description.narrative: The development objective of the Third Poverty Reduction Fund (PRF) Project for Lao People's Democratic Republic is to improve access to basic services for the Project's targeted poor communities. It will be achieved through inclusive community and local development processes with emphasis on ensuring sustainability. The project comprises of four components. The first component, community development sub-grants will finance carrying out of participatory community and local development planning processes at the village and Kum Ban levels; and provision of sub-grants for the implementation of eligible community infrastructure subprojects based on the Kum Ban development plans prepared under the Project. The second component, local and community development capacity building will finance provision of technical assistance to build the capacity of Kum Bans and villages to assess their needs and prepare Kum Ban development plans, and to plan, implement and monitor subprojects; provision of technical assistance to build the capacity of provincial and district authorities to facilitate community and local development planning processes and to support and supervise the development and implementation of subprojects; provision of technical assistance to the National Committee for Rural Development and Poverty Eradication to promote participatory rural development in coordination with various sector ministries and other entities supporting rural development in the Recipient's territory; Provision of technical and operational assistance for the development and implementation of partnerships between PRF and other agencies in rural sanitation, nutrition, poverty assessment, and other areas within the mandate of PRF; and Monitoring and evaluation of the activities carried out under part 1 and part 2 of the project. The third component, project management will finance the provision of technical and operational assistance for the day-to-day management of the project and the carrying out of financial audits. This will include remuneration of national, provincial and district PRF staff; associated equipment and operating costs; accounting, procurement, financial management (FM), internal controls, auditing, and other specialized areas. The fourth component, Nutrition Enhancing Livelihood Development will finance provision of capacity building assistance to village self-help group (SHGs), with a focus on women's SHGs in selected communities, to develop and implement nutrition sensitive livelihood activities and to enhance their knowledge of livelihood activities including financial literary and production cycles; monitoring and evaluation of the activities carried out under Part 3 of the Project, including carrying out of studies on thematic or operational innovations and participatory assessments of nutrition training.
To improve access to community-prioritized basic services as well as to support the production and consumption of nutritious foods in the Project's targeted poor communities.

title.narrative: % reduction in travel time from village center to kumban center due to road improvements

comment.narrative: Only roads connecting agricultural production sites to villages are financed under the additional financing. The project has therefore collected data to calculate the following indicator: Percentage change in travel time from agricultural production areas to village centers due to road improvements. This indicator should have been included in the RF at design of the additional financing. The Percentage change in travel time from agricultural production areas to villages centers due to road improvements and bridges is 40%. In 2024, 74 road projects were sampled while 54 were sampled in 2022, with average of reduction time to travel from production areas to village center by motorbike.. According to Final External Evaluation of PRF III (without AF) conducted in 2021 - the reduction due to road improvement was 58%.

title.narrative: # of communities able to plan, implement and monitor their Village Development Plans

comment.narrative: The definition was updating. There is a disconnect between the indicator and the definition, the definition is weak compared to what the indicator means (current definition: Number of villages that are trained by PRF to prepare village development plans). A community should be accounted for when the community is able to plan, implement and monitor their activities when it has fully completed a planned project with the support of a functional Village Implementation Team (fully functional to monitor activities). According to Final External Evaluation of PRF III (without the AF) conducted in 2021 - 1727 communities were able to plan, implement and monitor their VDPs.

comment.narrative: According to Final External Evaluation of PRF III (without the AF) conducted in 2021 - 92% of HHs in PRF beneficiary villages voting for village priorities.

title.narrative: % of PRF III sub-projects prioritized by ethnic group

comment.narrative: According to Final External Evaluation of PRF III (without the AF) conducted in 2021 - 88% of sub-projects were prioritized by ethnic groups.

title.narrative: % of households in PRF beneficiary villages satisfied with the participatory planning process supported by PRF III

comment.narrative: The previous data entered on April 2023 were affected by methodological errors. The last data were collected by an independent qualitative evaluation in 2022. Explanation of high result: the project has been successful at engaging the whole community for planning including women and ethnic minorities. However, the high achievement in terms of satisfaction could be due to the fact that beneficiaries are afraid of fully expressing their opinion in fear of not receiving benefits from future intervention/project. The results from 2024 focuses on PRF AF and were measured by an independent assessment. According to Final External Evaluation of PRF III (without the AF) conducted in 2021 - 95% of PRF beneficiary villages were satisfied with the participatory planning process.

title.narrative: % of PRF built infrastructure of functioning quality

comment.narrative: PRFIII was evaluated in the previous independent assessment funded by the World Bank for the Mid-Term Review (MTR), prior to the assessment conducted by student engineers.Due to significant delays in the construction of Additional Financing (AF) infrastructures, subsequent assessments, particularly independent ones, included a focus on these delays. However, limited funding necessitated a small, targeted sample for these assessments 93.8% (December 30, 2023): Survey conducted by final year students from faculty of civil engineering of the National University of Laos, focused on sub-projects financed during AF. 90% (May 25, 2024): Survey conducted by independent firm focused on sub-projects financed during AF. According to Final External Evaluation of PRF III (without the AF) conducted in 2021 - 94.6% of infrastructure was of functioning quality.

title.narrative: % of sub-projects of high technical quality

comment.narrative: Previous reporting from December 30, 2023 is 93.4% (survey conducted by final year students from faculty of civil engineering focused AF) and the current reporting from May 25, 2024 is 90% (survey conducted by independent firm focused on AF). Data reported on the indicator did not measure high quality as defined in the indicator, but just if standards were met (defined as good quality and fair) see last technical audit of infrastructures. The methodology was updated to match the AF. Assessing only roads, irrigation systems, small bridges, roofs for agricultural markets, fencing, storage and processing facilities No education, health and water infrastructures were assessed during the Additional Financing. According to Final External Evaluation of PRF III (without the AF) conducted in 2021 reported 92% of sub-projects of high quality.

title.narrative: % of registered grievances that are addressed according to agreed procedures
% of PRF III sub-project prioritized by women

comment.narrative: According to Final External Evaluation of PRF III (without the AF) conducted in 2021 - 94.90% of sub-projects were prioritized by women.

title.narrative: # of individuals using loans from Self Help Groups

comment.narrative: The data for the column for 2023 results has also been updated as 35,877.

The AF had initially planned to finance infrastructures in only 75% of villages, but as livelihood spending has been slow the project decided to reallocate some of the funds to finance infrastructures in 100% of villages. Some beneficiaries have benefited from both PRF and PRF additional financing (101 villages under both projects) and the project has paid particular attention to avoid double counting of the beneficiaries of both PRF and PRF additional financing. Under PRF III (without the AF) 690,000 Beneficiaries were reached.

title.narrative: Number of households who are members of Farmer Nutrition Groups

comment.narrative: The project has exceeded the target as farmer nutrition groups have enrolled more members (HH) than anticipated. Also, there are also more farmer nutrition groups than planned (530 versus 468) as some larger villages mobilized women and children into 2 to 3 groups in their respective hamlets. The project accounts for households. The data for the column for 2023 results has also been updated as 17,309.

The target proved to be too ambitious, as the methodology to calculate the target had some issues as the average live weight per animal was too high compared to the context of the project, where animals are leaner. At the time of the design of the project, the team did not recognize that not knowing in advance if Producer Groups (PGs) will undertake a livestock activity instead of crop will affect the results. In addition, inflation was at 33% and the cost of input has increased significantly, therefore it was not as commercially attractive to undertake livestock activities. The definition was modified since it did not originally include fish, but fish meat was produced by beneficiaries and has been reported.

title.narrative: % of Self Help Group members who take at least two loans

comment.narrative: The target was too ambitious.

title.narrative: Increase in hectares of irrigated area

comment.narrative: The impact of PRF AF has been more about improving the functioning of the existing irrigation schemes than expanding cropping areas under irrigation. The improvement in irrigation schemes has led to an increase in productivity and in the number of cropping seasons (in some cases leading to increase in cropping diversity). According to Final External Evaluation of PRF III (without the AF) conducted in 2021 - hectares of irrigated area was increased to 49.7%

title.narrative: % of Village Self-Help Group Management Committee (VSMC) members that are female

comment.narrative: The data for the column for 2023 results has also been updated as 81.2%.

title.narrative: % of Village Implementation Team (VIT) members that are female

comment.narrative: According to Final External Evaluation of PRF III (without the AF) conducted in 2021- 33.85% of VIT members were women.

title.narrative: Percentage of children 6–23 months from Farmer Nutrition Group households consuming foods from four or more recommended food groups

comment.narrative: Latest data for this indicator was collected by June 12, 2024, through a rapid survey financed by the WB; the quantitative data with a sample of 384 households was used as main data, along with IE data trends on dietary diversity in children 6-23 months applied by the nutrition convergence team.

title.narrative: Number of women selected for Road Maintenance Groups who earn an income, as a % of the number of poor households in village

comment.narrative: The formulation of the indicator was not clear and was updated in 2021 so that the project could report on on the the indicator. Previously the indicator was supposed to be measured only once with an IE by the Gender Lab, which ended up not measuring exactly this indicator (2020). It was last measured in 2021 by the project as the activity was still financed by SDC. It was measured as the Percentage of women selected for Road Maintenance Groups earning an income out of he number of poor households in targeted villages. The Final External Evaluation of PRF III (without the AF) conducted in 2021 reported 15.96%
